definition: In this historical language context, individual accuracy means the exactness with which a person reproduces speech sounds. Baldwin contrasts it with personal inaccuracy or variation in pronunciation, noting that when such individual variants spread through a community they can contribute to broader sound change.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Language; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not support defining "individual accuracy" as the exactness with which a person reproduces speech sounds; the source instead refers to "individual inaccuracies of pronunciation" and to "individual accuracy or aberration in reproduction" without defining the term as exactness.
The claim that Baldwin contrasts this with personal inaccuracy or variation in pronunciation is not directly supported by the packet as stated.

The statement that such variants spread through a community and contribute to broader sound change is broadly supported, but the requested sense of the term itself is not securely established by the source.

The definition states that “individual accuracy means the exactness with which a person reproduces speech sounds,” but the packet only says that sound-changes originate in “individual inaccuracies of pronunciation”; it does not define accuracy as “exactness” or describe reproduction of speech sounds in that way.

The definition attributes an explicit contrast (“Baldwin contrasts it with personal inaccuracy or variation in pronunciation”), but the packet mentions “individual inaccuracies of pronunciation” without clearly framing a contrast between defined terms “individual accuracy” and “personal inaccuracy.”

While the packet supports that individual inaccuracies can spread and contribute to broader sound change/tendency (“Only when these become frequent enough…to influence the community does a phonetic tendency develop…”), the definition’s wording includes additional concepts (exact reproduction; explicit contrasting framing) that are not supported by the packet.
